question.text: Metal deficiency defect is shown by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>Fe</mi><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>93</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></math>. In the crystal, some <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>Fe</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> cations are missing and loss of positive charge is compensated by the presence of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>Fe</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> ions. The percentage of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>Fe</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> ions in the<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>Fe</mi><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>93</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></math> crystals is____(Nearest integer)

solution.text:
In Fe0.93O for every 93Fe ions 14 are Fe+3 and 93-14=79 are Fe+2 ions

∴ %Fe+2=7993×100=84.9%

∴ nearest integer =85%
